feed.title: Science & Academia — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Agriculture
entry.summary: A list of open-source technology and tools for farming and gardening. Unlike commercial agriculture software, it gathers only open-source options — sensors, irrigation, farm management, data.

entry.title: Awesome Bioinformatics
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for analysing biological data (bioinformatics). Unlike general data-science lists, it focuses on biology-specific tools such as sequence alignment and variant calling.

entry.title: Awesome Citizen Science
entry.summary: A list for community-based, non-institutional science (citizen science). Unlike academic science resources, it gathers projects, tools and hardware open to people outside institutions.

entry.title: Awesome Clean Tech
entry.summary: A list of projects and resources fighting climate change with technology. Unlike general sustainability writing, it focuses on open-source projects and areas where developers can contribute.

entry.title: Awesome Computational Biology
entry.summary: A list of resources for computational approaches to biology problems. Unlike tool-heavy bioinformatics lists, it pairs courses, books and methods with the tools.

entry.title: Awesome Healthcare
entry.summary: A list of open-source healthcare software for facilities. Unlike commercial health software, it gathers open-source options — electronic health records, imaging, standards such as HL7/FHIR.

entry.title: Awesome Information Retrieval
entry.summary: A list of information-retrieval resources for learning to build your own search engine. Unlike the docs of ready engines such as Elasticsearch, it teaches the theory underneath — indexing, ranking, evaluation.

entry.title: Awesome LaTeX
entry.summary: A list of packages, templates and tools for LaTeX, the scientific typesetting language. Unlike Overleaf’s docs, it gathers editors, packages and templates without tying them to one service.

entry.title: Awesome Neuroimaging
entry.summary: A list of imaging software for analysing brain data from living subjects. Unlike general image-processing lists, it focuses on software specific to brain data such as MRI and fMRI.

entry.title: Awesome Neuroscience
entry.summary: A list of computational resources for studying the nervous system and brain. Unlike the neuroimaging list, it focuses on computational modelling, data sources and courses rather than imaging.

entry.title: Awesome Quarto
entry.summary: A resource list for Quarto, the scientific and technical open-source publishing system. Unlike R Markdown it is language-agnostic: you write the same document with Python, R, Julia or Observable.

entry.title: Awesome Scientific Computing
entry.summary: A list of tools and libraries for solving complex scientific problems by computer. Unlike data-science lists, it focuses on numerical methods — finite elements, linear algebra, differential-equation solvers.

entry.title: Awesome Theoretical CS
entry.summary: A list for the interplay of computer science and pure mathematics (theoretical CS). Unlike practical programming lists, it covers theoretical fields such as complexity theory, algorithm analysis and logic.

entry.title: Begin LaTeX in Minutes
entry.summary: A brief intro to LaTeX for beginners, in minutes. Unlike Overleaf’s long guides it is a one-page quick start: document structure, maths, tables and bibliography basics.

entry.title: DBLP
entry.summary: The open bibliography database of computer science publications, with tidy author pages and conference volumes. Against Google Scholar it is clean and hand-maintained — author ambiguity and phantom records are rare.

entry.title: Computer History Museum
entry.summary: Oral history interviews with the pioneers of computing, plus a lecture archive. Unlike technical channels it records the circumstances a decision was made in — the context no document holds.

entry.title: Nature
entry.summary: One of science’s most prestigious peer-reviewed journals, carrying news and research together. Unlike preprint archives its strict peer review gives published findings their weight.

entry.title: OpenStax
entry.summary: A Rice University project offering university textbooks free and openly licensed. Unlike commercial texts it gives full, peer-reviewed volumes that are free and regularly updated.

entry.title: PhET Simulations
entry.summary: The University of Colorado’s interactive simulations for physics, chemistry and maths. Unlike a lecture it lets you experience a concept by tweaking its parameters by hand.

entry.title: Semantic Scholar
entry.summary: An AI-powered academic search engine. Unlike Google Scholar it summarises a paper, distinguishes influential citations and extracts links semantically.

entry.title: Connected Papers
entry.summary: A tool that starts from one paper and builds a visual graph of related work. Unlike a citation list it draws a “map” of a field and shows neighbouring work.

entry.title: SKYbrary
entry.summary: An EUROCONTROL-backed aviation safety knowledge base of accident analyses, human factors and safety management systems. Unlike general aviation sites it focuses on safety — a usable archive for anyone thinking about high-reliability system design.

entry.title: İÜ Gazete Arşivi
entry.summary: Istanbul University’s scanned historical newspaper collection. Unlike secondary literature it is a primary source, where the details that literature skips turn up.

entry.title: Nişanyan Yeradları
entry.summary: A historical inventory of settlement names in and around Turkey. Unlike official place-name lists, it documents former names and every change with date and source — nothing else compiles this systematically.

entry.title: David Rumsey Harita Koleksiyonu
entry.summary: A high-resolution historical map archive. Unlike plain scanned collections, it lets you georeference maps onto modern geography — a strong tool for tracking place-name and border change.

entry.title: Transkribus · Osmanlıca
entry.summary: A text-recognition model trained on printed Ottoman Turkish. Unlike general OCR tools it can read Arabic-script Turkish — a gap that is critical in archive research.

entry.title: ABD Antarktika Programı
entry.summary: The official portal of the US Antarctic research programme, with material on field logistics and station operations. Unlike general science news, it details how systems are operated in extreme conditions.

entry.title: Devlet Arşivleri
entry.summary: Turkey’s official archive institution and the gateway to catalogues and digital copies of Ottoman and Republican-era documents. Unlike secondary sources, it takes you to the original document.

entry.title: Aperta
entry.summary: TÜBİTAK’s open archive, hosting research data alongside publications. Data sharing is not yet common in Turkey, which makes it notable.

entry.title: Harman
entry.summary: A harvester searching Turkey’s institutional academic archives from one place. Instead of hunting for theses and articles university by university, one search covers them all.

entry.title: DergiPark
entry.summary: The open-access platform for Turkish academic journals, hosting over a thousand titles — the primary source for Turkish literature, not aggregated anywhere else.

entry.title: Wolfram Alpha
entry.summary: A computational knowledge engine that integrates, converts units and compares data. Unlike a search engine it computes the answer rather than finding it, showing the working step by step in the paid tier.

entry.title: iNaturalist
entry.summary: Share nature observations and get species identified. Unlike species-ID apps it has community verification: confirmed records become research-grade and flow into GBIF — a rare case of a hobby producing real data.

entry.title: Ethnologue
entry.summary: The standard catalogue of world languages with systematic speaker counts and vitality ratings, and the registration authority for ISO 639-3 codes. Unlike Wikipedia it offers systematic data; detailed access is paid.

entry.title: Open Language Archives Community
entry.summary: A community uniting language resource archives under a shared metadata standard. Unlike the search page this is the infrastructure side — the standard and participant list that make scattered university collections searchable.

entry.title: Open Language Archives (arama)
entry.summary: Searches language resources across scattered institutional archives from one place. Instead of trawling archives one by one, you find material — especially on under-documented and endangered languages — in one search.

entry.title: Vikipedi Portalları
entry.summary: An index of Wikipedia’s topic portals — a structured way into a field instead of random search, and a way not to enter a new subject without a map.

entry.title: Arkhe Projesi
entry.summary: Turkish science and philosophy writing. Unlike popular-science sites it does not stay shallow, and unlike academic papers it is not written in an opaque register.

entry.title: SkyViewer
entry.summary: Browses sky survey data by position, letting you overlay telescope imagery and compare across wavelengths.

entry.title: Oxford Academic
entry.summary: Oxford University Press’s journal platform, one of the major publisher archives. Compared with open-access archives most content is behind subscription, with open-access articles separately marked.
